stops.title: Point Lines: connect and measure
stops.makes: You join A and B, compute b - a and its length, and show the distance as text while either end moves.

notes.text: The kit's `line.gd` is indented with tabs, and the code on this page uses spaces. Godot accepts either, but not both in one file. A line pasted with spaces into `line.gd` stops the whole script with `Parse Error: Used space character for indentation instead of tab as used before in the file.`, and the study runs without it: A and B sit at the middle of the floor. Indent with the Tab key instead.

Reversing the subtraction changes nothing you can see. `segment.gd` does its own subtraction from A and B, and the length is the same either way. To see the direction reverse, add `print(displacement)` on the line under `var displacement := b - a`. The Output panel fills with `(1.5, 0.0, 0.0)`, one line per frame. Change `b - a` to `a - b`, and it prints `(-1.5, 0.0, 0.0)`, while the segment and the readout stay as they were. Put back `b - a` and remove the print.

notes.at: Read again as the endpoints move
notes.text: To use the Remote scene tree: run the study from the editor, then click **Remote** at the top of the Scene dock. Open the tree under `root`, select `B`, and change its **Position** in the Inspector. The segment and the number follow. **Local** returns to the saved scene. *(editor: these clicks are described, not watched)*

stops.title: Break it on purpose, then look it up
stops.makes: You break scripts that work, predict each error, read Godot's exact message, fix it, and look a method up in the class reference.
stops.status_note: Every message on this page comes from a Godot 4.6 run. The editor's panels are described, not watched.

verified.native: 2026-09-30 Godot 4.6, headless and with the command-line debugger (-d) driven through each stop: every case run in a fresh copy of the point-zero, point-lines or point-trace kit, every quoted message, warning, debugger stop and backtrace reproduced.

teacher.why_here: Debugging should come in through small constructions the learner already owns, not wait for an appendix. By Trace the learner has met paths, types, lists and a function that calls another, so each has a loud failure worth reading. The project's own common failures are quiet, so the loud cases come first, and the quiet ones close the workshop.
teacher.status_detail: Rewritten 2026-09-30: every case starts from a fresh kit copy; runtime cases lead with the debugger stop; the list faults moved into a point-trace copy (a wrong literal, the empty-list guard removed, pop_back for pop_front). Debugger behaviour was measured with Godot's command-line debugger, which attaches as the editor's does, by sending continue and bt through a pipe: a SCRIPT ERROR in _process stops again after each continue; one in _ready does not; ERROR lines never stop the game. Warnings (unused variable, narrowing conversion) print only with a debugger attached. The editor's Debugger panel, script editor and Search Help were not watched.
teacher.check: Each message you predicted appears, and names a line at or near the fault. Parse errors appear before the scene runs. A SCRIPT ERROR stops its function and, from the editor, pauses the game at its line; an ERROR is printed and the game goes on.
teacher.contrast: A fault with no error, such as a readout that shows the wrong number, is found by watching a value. Sometimes a warning points at it first; pop_back in the recorder leaves none.
teacher.carries: A debugging habit that starts from a prediction, the difference between an error, a warning and silence, and the class reference as the first place to look.
teacher.learner_room: Plant one fault of your own in a copy of your study, give it to someone, and time how long they take to find it.
